transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, mostly I'm here because I'm just so... tired. But it's not a normal tired. It's a tired that sleep doesn't fix at all. Like, even doing something simple, like unloading the dishwasher, feels like climbing a mountain. Or reading for my certificate class—I'm taking this online course, you know, just trying to finish up some college credits I started years ago. I was actually doing really well in my history class back then, I had this professor who was obsessed with the Roman Empire, and he would always bring in these little artifacts... Anyway, yeah, even just trying to read a chapter for my class now just feels like way too much. I just don't have the energy for it.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you used to, even activities you normally like?

Yeah, exactly. It's like I just stopped caring about the things that usually make me feel like myself. I usually love sketching, going to gallery openings, cooking, yoga... or even just playing tennis with a friend. Actually, my friend Jessica just bought this ridiculous neon green tennis racket. She got it at that massive new sporting goods store by the highway. Have you seen it? It's huge. They have this giant rock-climbing wall right in the middle of the store, which just seems like a massive liability if you ask me. I mean, what if some kid falls off? I broke my arm falling off a swing set in third grade and my mom tried to sue the school, but that went nowhere. She was always trying to sue somebody back then, she had this lawyer on speed dial... But, um, what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, Jessica wanted to play tennis this weekend and I just... I couldn't even bring myself to text her back. I just don't have the interest in any of it right now.
How long have you been feeling this way?

I think it's been about three months now. Yeah, because it started right around the time my apartment complex decided to repaint all the front doors. They sent out this passive-aggressive memo saying they were updating the community aesthetic, but they chose this awful shade of red. It was supposed to be cranberry, but honestly, it just looks like dried ketchup. And the painters were so sloppy, they left that blue painter's tape over my peephole for a whole week. I had to scrape it off myself with a butter knife. My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, she complained to the management company literally every single day. She’s lived there for twenty years, so she acts like she owns the building, and she has this little yappy dog that just barks at the wind... but, um, anyway. Yeah, it's been about three months of just this... quiet, heavy stretch where I'm just too tired and don't have any interest in doing much of anything.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently?

Yeah, actually, my appetite has been pretty off. I'll get to the end of the day and suddenly realize I've only had coffee and maybe a few bites of something. Speaking of coffee, this new place just opened up on my corner, one of those super pretentious spots where the baristas wear leather aprons? I went in there and the guy making my drink had this crazy handlebar mustache, like a 19th-century villain. Like he was about to tie somebody to the train tracks, you know? I don't even understand how you drink anything with a mustache like that, it just seems like a massive hygiene issue. My uncle had a mustache like that in the nineties and he always got soup in it, which was just disgusting to watch at Thanksgiving. He would always bring this awful green bean casserole, too, with those crispy onions on top... but, um... wait, what was the question? Oh, weight. Right. Yeah, so because I haven't really been eating, my jeans have gotten a lot looser lately. I'm definitely not trying to lose weight or anything, they just don't fit right anymore.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the past few months?

Yeah, pretty much. Just this heavy, down feeling that won't go away. It's like this cloud that just sits there all day, every day. It's funny you mention clouds, actually, because the weather has been so bizarre lately. Yesterday it was pouring rain, just absolutely dumping buckets, and then twenty minutes later the sun was out and it was freezing. I was trying to walk to the pharmacy because I needed to pick up some more of that fancy toothpaste I like—the one with the charcoal in it? I know people say it ruins your enamel, but I swear it makes my teeth whiter. Anyway, I didn't have an umbrella because I left it on the subway last week. It was a really nice umbrella, too, one of those ones that pushes a button and it pops open automatically. I got it at this little boutique downtown that sells all these imported Japanese stationery supplies. They have these pens that write so smoothly, I could just doodle with them for hours... wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, feeling down. Yeah, it's been pretty constant. Most of the day, every day, just feeling really low.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, have you been more restless or fidgety than usual?

Well, it's definitely not restless. It's more like... on my slower days, it feels like my body is moving through wet cement. Like everything is just dragging. I actually walked past a construction site the other day where they were pouring a new sidewalk, and the smell of the wet cement was so strong. It reminded me of when I was a kid and my dad poured a new patio in our backyard. We all put our handprints in it, and my brother tried to push his toy dinosaur into the concrete so it would look like a fossil. He was obsessed with dinosaurs back then, specifically the triceratops. He had this whole collection of plastic ones, and he'd leave them all over the living room floor. Stepping on a plastic triceratops barefoot in the middle of the night is honestly worse than stepping on a Lego. I still have a scar on my heel from it, I think... but, um... what was I saying? Oh, right, moving slowly. Yeah, it's just really hard to get going. Even answering a simple question from my spouse can take me a weirdly long time, like my brain is just buffering.
Have you ever felt so low that you've thought about hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living?

No, I haven't really had thoughts like that. I mean, I feel terrible, but I don't want to hurt myself. I've never been the kind of person who could even handle pain very well. When I was in college, I went to get my ears pierced for a second time, just the lobes, nothing crazy. My roommate at the time convinced me to go to this place in the mall, which I knew was a bad idea because they use those awful piercing guns instead of needles. She insisted it was fine because she got her cartilage done there and it healed perfectly. Well, mine got so infected I had to take the earrings out after three days. It throbbed constantly, like a heartbeat in my earlobe. I ended up having to use this special saline spray, which honestly smelled a little bit like the ocean. I love the ocean, though. We used to go to Cape Cod every summer when I was little, and we'd collect sea glass on the beach... wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, hurting myself. No, no thoughts like that. Just feeling really down.
Has there been a time recently when nothing — not even things you usually enjoy — felt pleasurable or interesting to you at all?

Yeah, definitely. It's like I just completely stopped caring about the things that usually make me feel like myself. I haven't wanted to do any of it... sketching, cooking, yoga. Even going to gallery openings or playing tennis with a friend, which I usually love. Actually, my tennis racket has been sitting by the front door for weeks, and my cat keeps chewing on the grip tape. He's a rescue, an orange tabby, and he has this weird obsession with anything rubber or foam. The vet said it's a condition where they chew on non-food items. Last year, he swallowed a piece of my foam roller, and we had to take him to the emergency vet at 2 AM. Have you ever been to an emergency vet? It's so chaotic. There was a woman in the waiting room with a parrot wrapped in a towel, and the parrot kept whistling the theme song to The Andy Griffith Show. It was surreal. I didn't even know birds could learn whole songs like that, though I guess I've seen those videos online of cockatoos dancing to pop music. They have such surprisingly good rhythm, it's kind of fascinating how their brains process a beat... um... wait, what were we talking about? Sorry, my mind just went totally blank. Oh, right, enjoying things. Yeah, I just haven't had the interest for any of my usual stuff. Nothing sounds fun at all.
Before this current period of feeling down, have you had any other episodes in the past where you felt this way for at least two weeks?

I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days before, obviously, but nothing that lasted that long. Usually, if I have a bad day, I just try to sleep it off. Sleep is so important, you know? I was reading this article the other day about circadian rhythms and how blue light from our phones completely messes them up. I actually bought these blue-light blocking glasses online, but they make everything look weirdly yellow, like you're in an old sepia photograph. My grandmother had this huge album of sepia photographs from when her parents immigrated from Italy. They came over on a boat in the 1920s, and she had the actual passenger manifest with their names on it. It's crazy to think about traveling across the ocean like that, just on a boat for weeks with no idea what you're walking into. I get seasick just going on the ferry to Staten Island. The last time I took it, I had to stand outside the whole time because the smell of the snack bar inside was making me nauseous. They were selling these giant pretzels that looked like they'd been sitting under a heat lamp since 1995. I can't stand old bread... um... wait, what was the question? Oh, past episodes. No, I don't remember feeling this bad for two whole weeks before.
Before this current period of feeling down, have you ever had any other times in your life where you felt this way for at least two weeks at a time?

I think... wait, didn't you just ask me that? Or something really similar? But yeah, like I was just saying, no, I really don't think I've ever felt this bad for two whole weeks before. Two weeks is kind of a long time to keep track of how you're feeling anyway. I usually lose track of days unless I write everything down. 

I actually bought this really beautiful planner at the beginning of the year to try and be more organized. It had these gorgeous watercolor hydrangeas on the cover. Hydrangeas are my absolute favorite flower, they remind me of my aunt's house in Connecticut. She had this massive garden in her backyard, and the soil there was so acidic that all the hydrangeas turned this deep, vibrant blue. I read once that you can change the color of them by putting coffee grounds in the dirt. I tried doing that with a potted plant I had on my balcony once, but I think I just ended up attracting a bunch of fruit flies. Fruit flies are the absolute worst, once you get them in your kitchen, they just never leave. You have to make those little traps with apple cider vinegar and dish soap, but then your whole apartment just smells like salad dressing... 

Um, sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? Losing my train of thought. But yeah, to answer your question again, no, I haven't had this happen before this current time.
Before this current period of feeling down, have you ever had any other times in your life where you felt this way for at least two weeks at a time?

You definitely just asked me that, didn't you? Yeah, you did. I feel like we're going in circles a little bit here. But no, I haven't. Like I said, two weeks is a really long time to just be miserable. I mean, who has the time for that anyway? 

I used to work with this girl, Sarah, at this boutique downtown, and she was always miserable. Just constantly complaining about everything—the music the manager played, the lighting, the customers. She actually got into a screaming match with a customer once over a return policy on a silk scarf. It was one of those really delicate, hand-painted ones, and the lady had clearly worn it and spilled, like, red wine or something on it. Red wine stains are impossible to get out. My mom swears by club soda and salt, but I think that's an old wives' tale. I spilled some Pinot Noir on my favorite white rug last New Year's Eve, and I tried everything. Baking soda, vinegar, those expensive carpet cleaners in the spray bottles... nothing worked. I ended up just having to put a coffee table over the stain to hide it. It's a nice coffee table, though, mid-century modern, I got it at this flea market in Brooklyn. The guy selling it said it belonged to a jazz musician in the 70s, which is probably a lie, but it makes for a good story, you know? Jazz is so interesting, the way it's all improvised. I tried to learn the saxophone when I was in middle school, but I didn't have the lung capacity... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Right, the two weeks thing. Yeah, no. Never happened before this.
Have you ever had any other times in your life, before this current period, when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks at a time?

Okay, are you messing with me? Because I swear this is the fourth time you've asked me the exact same thing. Did you ask me that? Am I going crazy? I feel like I'm in that movie Groundhog Day. Have you seen that? Bill Murray is so funny in it, just waking up to "I Got You Babe" over and over again. Sonny and Cher had such a weird dynamic, don't you think? Like, he was so much older than her, and then she went on to have this massive solo career and wear all those crazy Bob Mackie outfits. I saw one of her dresses at a museum exhibit once, and it was entirely made of crystals. It must have weighed like fifty pounds. I can't imagine trying to perform in something that heavy. I wore a beaded dress to a wedding once, and by the end of the night, my shoulders were covered in bruises. It was my cousin's wedding, actually, the one who married a guy she met on a snorkeling trip in Hawaii. They had a destination wedding in Maui, which sounds great until you realize how expensive flights are. I had to put the whole trip on a credit card that I'm still paying off. Credit card interest rates are practically extortion these days. I was listening to a podcast about personal finance, and they said... 

Wait. The question. The two weeks thing. No. I haven't. I really, really haven't. Like I said the last three times.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks in a row?

Okay, seriously, is there a hidden camera in here? Because I feel like I'm being punked. You've definitely asked me this exact same question like five times now. Is this some kind of memory test? Because my memory is usually pretty good, unless I'm trying to remember where I put my keys. I lose my keys constantly. I even bought one of those little Bluetooth trackers you put on your keychain, but then the battery died and I kept forgetting to buy the little coin batteries for it. You can't just buy those at the grocery store anymore, you have to go to a specialty electronics place or order them online. And when you order them online, they come in this massive cardboard box with all that plastic bubble wrap for something that's the size of a quarter. It's so wasteful. I've been trying to reduce my plastic use, actually. I bought these reusable silicone storage bags for my leftovers, but they're so hard to wash. You have to prop them open on a drying rack or they get all mildewy inside, and mildew is just disgusting... 

But anyway, to answer your question again, no. I've never felt this way for two weeks straight before this. I promise.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks in a row?

Okay, I'm starting to think you're not listening to me at all. Or maybe you're a robot? Are you a robot? Because this is literally the exact same question you just asked me, and the time before that, and the time before that. It's like a broken record. Have you ever seen a real record player? My dad had one, a vintage Marantz, and he was obsessed with it. He had crates and crates of vinyl, mostly classic rock like Led Zeppelin and Pink Floyd. He used to make me sit and listen to "Dark Side of the Moon" with him, all the way through, without talking. He said you had to listen to the whole album as a complete piece of art, not just the singles. I get it, I guess, but I'm more of a playlist person myself. I like to mix it up. I have a playlist for everything—working out, cleaning the house, driving. Speaking of driving, the traffic on the way here was a nightmare. There was some kind of construction on the highway, and they had three lanes merged into one. It took me an extra forty-five minutes just to get through it. I don't understand why they always do construction during rush hour. Shouldn't they do it in the middle of the night when no one is on the road? It just makes so much more sense...

But yeah, the two weeks thing. For the millionth time, no. Never. Not before this.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks in a row?

Are you... are you actually serious right now? I'm honestly looking around for the hidden cameras because this is getting ridiculous. You're asking me the exact same thing again! It's like that movie, 50 First Dates, where Drew Barrymore wakes up every day and forgets everything. Have you seen it? Adam Sandler is so sweet in it, trying to make her fall in love with him every single day. I love Hawaii, too. That's where it's set. I've always wanted to go to Oahu and see the North Shore, maybe watch the surfing competitions. I tried surfing once in California, but the water was freezing. Even with a wetsuit, I was shivering so hard my teeth were chattering. Plus, I kept falling off the board. It's way harder than it looks on TV. You need so much core strength to just pop up on the board, let alone ride a wave. I started doing Pilates to try and build my core, but the reformer machine is so intimidating. It looks like some kind of medieval torture device with all the springs and straps. The instructor was really nice, though, she kept telling me to breathe into my ribs, which is such a weird concept. How do you breathe into your ribs? You breathe into your lungs...

Anyway. Look. I don't know how else to say this to you. No. The answer is still no. I have not had a time like that before this. Never.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks in a row?

Okay, I am officially losing my mind. Or you are. Is there something wrong with your computer? Like, is a glitch just spitting out the same prompt over and over? Because I've answered this, I swear to you, I've answered this so many times now. It's like being stuck in a loop. Have you ever played one of those video games where you have to keep re-doing the same level until you get it exactly right? My nephew plays this game, I think it's called Hades, and he just dies over and over and over again, but he says that's the whole point of the game. You're supposed to die so you can learn the pattern. It seems so frustrating to me. I prefer games where you actually build something, like The Sims. I used to spend hours designing houses on The Sims, picking out the wallpaper and the furniture. I'd make these massive mansions with indoor pools and bowling alleys. But then I'd get bored once the house was built and I actually had to make the little people go to work and take out the trash. The real-life simulation part is just too much like... well, real life. Taking out the trash is the worst chore. The bags always leak, and then you have to scrub the bottom of the can...

But look. Doctor. Please listen to me. I have never felt down or lost interest for two weeks straight before this current thing. Okay? Never. Can we please talk about something else now?
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks in a row?

Are you actually messing with me right now? Is someone feeding you lines through an earpiece? Because this is literally insane. It's like I'm on one of those old prank shows. Remember Punk'd? With Ashton Kutcher and the trucker hats? I never understood the trucker hat phase. My college roommate, Sarah, she had this neon pink Von Dutch hat that she wore to literally everything. Even when we went to this super fancy Italian place for her birthday. The waiters kept giving us the dirtiest looks. The food wasn't even that good, honestly. I ordered the chicken parmesan and it was mostly just burnt breading. I make way better chicken parm at home. The trick is to mix a little bit of parmesan cheese right into the breadcrumbs before you fry it, and you have to use a cast iron skillet. Cast iron is the best, but it's so heavy to wash. I dropped mine on my toe once and thought I broke it. I had to wear flip-flops for a week, which was awful because it was raining and my feet kept slipping out of them... 

But anyway. Read my lips, doctor. No. Zero. Never. I never had a two-week period like that before this one. If you ask me this one more time, I think I might actually scream.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks in a row?

Okay, I am... I'm actually screaming inside right now. Did you just ask me that again? Is this a test? Like some psychological experiment where you see how many times you can repeat the exact same sentence before the patient snaps? Because my psychology professor in college, Dr. Henderson, he talked about these kinds of experiments. He was obsessed with the Milgram experiment, the one with the electric shocks? He brought it up in almost every single lecture. He had this really weird, high-pitched laugh that always sounded like he was nervous, even when he wasn't. We used to try and count how many times he laughed during a 50-minute class. My friend Mark sat next to me, and he'd keep a tally on the back of his notebook. Mark was hilarious, he could do impressions of almost anyone. His best one was Christopher Walken. He'd order pizza as Christopher Walken, and the delivery guys never knew how to react. I love pizza, but I can't do the deep dish kind. It's just too much bread, you know? It feels more like a casserole than a pizza. New York style is the best, where you can fold the slice in half. I went to New York once for a long weekend, and we walked so much my calves were sore for three days. We walked all the way across the Brooklyn Bridge...

But seriously. Doctor. I am begging you. No. I have not. I have never, ever, ever felt down or lost interest for two weeks before this. I don't have that to tell you. Can we please, please move on?
